title: Identify Most Liked Content Posts
description_markdown: Engagement team request: For each post in `posts`, count total likes received in `likes` as `like_count`. Return `p.post_id`, `u.handle AS author_handle`, and `like_count`. Filter for `like_count >= 1`. Order by `like_count` DESC, `p.post_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Most liked posts
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT p.post_id, u.handle AS author_handle, COUNT(l.like_id) AS like_count FROM posts p JOIN social_users u ON p.user_id = u.user_id JOIN likes l ON p.post_id = l.post_id GROUP BY p.post_id, u.handle HAVING COUNT(l.like_id) >= 1 ORDER BY like_count DESC, p.post_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Joins posts to reactions and user handles.
hints: Join posts -> users and posts -> likes.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT p.post_id, u.handle AS author_handle, COUNT(l.like_id) AS like_count FROM posts p JOIN social_users u ON p.user_id = u.user_id JOIN likes l ON p.post_id = l.post_id GROUP BY p.post_id, u.handle HAVING COUNT(l.like_id) >= 1 ORDER BY like_count DESC, p.post_id ASC;

title: Calculate User Follower Popularity
description_markdown: Growth team request: Count how many followers each user has in `follows` as `follower_count`. Return `u.user_id`, `u.handle`, and `follower_count`. Order by `follower_count` DESC, `u.user_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Follower count per user

solution_query: SELECT u.user_id, u.handle, COUNT(f.follower_id) AS follower_count FROM social_users u LEFT JOIN follows f ON u.user_id = f.following_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.handle ORDER BY follower_count DESC, u.user_id ASC;
solution_explanation: LEFT JOIN on `f.following_id` counts how many other profiles follow this user.

title: Detect Bidirectional Mutual Follow Relationships
description_markdown: Graph network request: Find all pairs of users who mutually follow each other. Return `f1.follower_id AS user_a`, `f1.following_id AS user_b`. Ensure `user_a < user_b` to eliminate reciprocal duplicates. Order by `user_a` ASC, `user_b` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Mutual follow self-join
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT f1.follower_id AS user_a, f1.following_id AS user_b FROM follows f1 JOIN follows f2 ON f1.follower_id = f2.following_id AND f1.following_id = f2.follower_id WHERE f1.follower_id < f1.following_id ORDER BY user_a ASC, user_b ASC;
solution_explanation: Self-joins the graph adjacency table to locate symmetric edges `(A -> B AND B -> A)`.
hints: Join `ON f1.follower_id = f2.following_id AND f1.following_id = f2.follower_id`.
Filter `f1.follower_id < f1.following_id`.

Query: SELECT f1.follower_id AS user_a, f1.following_id AS user_b FROM follows f1 JOIN follows f2 ON f1.follower_id = f2.following_id AND f1.following_id = f2.follower_id WHERE f1.follower_id < f1.following_id ORDER BY user_a ASC, user_b ASC;

title: Aggregate Total Engagements Across Likes and Comments
description_markdown: For each post, compute `total_likes`, `total_comments`, and `total_engagements` (likes + comments) using `COUNT(DISTINCT)`. Return `post_id`, `total_likes`, `total_comments`, and `total_engagements`. Order by `total_engagements` DESC, `post_id` ASC.

Query: SELECT p.post_id, COUNT(DISTINCT l.like_id) AS total_likes, COUNT(DISTINCT c.comment_id) AS total_comments, (COUNT(DISTINCT l.like_id) + COUNT(DISTINCT c.comment_id)) AS total_engagements FROM posts p LEFT JOIN likes l ON p.post_id = l.post_id LEFT JOIN comments c ON p.post_id = c.post_id GROUP BY p.post_id ORDER BY total_engagements DESC, p.post_id ASC;

title: Compile User Engagement Activity Scorecard
description_markdown: Compile user activity metrics: `handle`, `posts_count`, `comments_count`, and `likes_given` using `COUNT(DISTINCT)`. Order by `posts_count` DESC, `comments_count` DESC, `likes_given` DESC, `handle` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Write your solution query here

solution_query: SELECT u.handle, COUNT(DISTINCT p.post_id) AS posts_count, COUNT(DISTINCT c.comment_id) AS comments_count, COUNT(DISTINCT l.like_id) AS likes_given FROM social_users u LEFT JOIN posts p ON u.user_id = p.user_id LEFT JOIN comments c ON u.user_id = c.user_id LEFT JOIN likes l ON u.user_id = l.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.handle ORDER BY posts_count DESC, comments_count DESC, likes_given DESC, u.handle ASC;
solution_explanation: LEFT JOINs posts, comments, and likes with COUNT(DISTINCT) to prevent multiplicative joins.
hints: Use `COUNT(DISTINCT p.post_id)`, `COUNT(DISTINCT c.comment_id)`, and `COUNT(DISTINCT l.like_id)`.
Group by `u.user_id, u.handle`.

Query: SELECT u.handle, COUNT(DISTINCT p.post_id) AS posts_count, COUNT(DISTINCT c.comment_id) AS comments_count, COUNT(DISTINCT l.like_id) AS likes_given FROM social_users u LEFT JOIN posts p ON u.user_id = p.user_id LEFT JOIN comments c ON u.user_id = c.user_id LEFT JOIN likes l ON u.user_id = l.user_id GROUP BY u.user_id, u.handle ORDER BY posts_count DESC, comments_count DESC, likes_given DESC, u.handle ASC;
